## Motivation

Cloud automations can refresh before the initial GitHub account is available, showing a sign-in or load error to an already signed-in user. Wait for account initialization and represent that period as loading, while preserving real signed-out, enterprise, and catalogue failures.

## Changes

- Await default-account initialization before the read-refresh unavailable gate, and reconcile the inner store when initialization finishes even without an account-change event.
- Expose enabled providers awaiting their initial account as `loading`, keeping the existing visible and accessible load-error output synchronized.
- Preserve strict mutation checks, signed-out and enterprise rejection, independent history readiness, and Refresh/sign-in recovery paths; refresh is not gated on catalogue readiness or creation eligibility.
- Add regressions for a late initial account without an event, retry after catalogue failure, history-only failure, signed-out/enterprise accounts, and loading versus real errors in visual and accessible output.

All changes are within automations. This does not retain cached automations across account/client replacement or redesign provider reconnection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cloud automations initialize with an enabled provider while the default GitHub account is still loading
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The automation catalogue remains loading until the existing default-account initialization barrier resolves; then store construction and its initial definition/history refresh must complete before catalogue data is ready. This does not block general workbench startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve recent local workspaces to GitHub repositories by reading git configuration during the first catalogue refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per recent workspace during this refresh, with repositories deduplicated by owner/name before remote reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For the specific late-account-without-event case, the adapter remained unavailable and never reached this refresh; ordinary account-change initialization already performed the same work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Repository resolution is on the catalogue refresh critical path after account initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the GitHub account client, verify each repository, list paginated automation definitions, hydrate summaries, and fetch bounded run history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository verification plus up to ten list pages and one detail read per returned definition for each deduplicated repository; history performs one bounded list per definition and detail reads only for active tasks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The late-account-without-event case incorrectly issued no requests; normal account-event initialization already issued the identical bounded/coalesced refresh sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Definition requests, followed by history requests, determine when the initial automation catalogue and history become ready.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One default cloud-automation provider; downstream work scales with deduplicated stored and recent GitHub repositories, pages of definitions per repository, and definitions whose run history is queried.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The account promise is created once. GitHubCloudAutomationStore coalesces concurrent definition refreshes with refreshPromise, serializes operations through a Sequencer, processes repositories serially, hydrates definition details in batches of five, and limits history work to four definitions concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The account initialization promise is retained for the store lifetime and is immediate after warm initialization. The GitHub client acquisition is coalesced per account lifetime; definition and history refreshes are coalesced while in flight. Account/client changes dispose the old store and invalidate its caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added observable dependency creates the store after the initialization barrier, and the traced store code proves the downstream filesystem/network cardinality, serialization, limits, and coalescing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of recent/stored repositories and definitions varies, but the diff adds only the single refresh needed to make this previously skipped product path functional and preserves existing caps and coalescing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new work restores the intended one-time refresh after a late account appears; it does not add avoidable repeated work or unbounded fan-out relative to the existing initialized-account path.

Scenarios.Scenario: User invokes Refresh while default-account initialization is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command now waits for the account initialization barrier, then the cloud provider refreshes definitions and history before the command completes. Waiting is necessary to avoid an immediate unavailable failure; other providers in ProviderAutomationService refresh concurrently through Promise.all.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh GitHub automation definitions and history after the account becomes available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced definition sequence and one coalesced history sequence despite the automatic and manual callers; effective request count follows deduplicated repositories and definitions, not caller count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A refresh after an already initialized account performed the same calls. During late initialization it previously failed before any call; the diff delays it until the provider can perform its normal refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The manual Refresh command waits for these remote calls and surfaces their completion/error.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One refresh invocation, potentially overlapping the adapter's automatic post-initialization refresh; downstream scale is the deduplicated repository and automation cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Both callers converge on GitHubCloudAutomationStore.refreshPromise for definitions and CloudAutomationStore.historyRefresh for history, so overlap produces one definition refresh and one history refresh rather than duplicate boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold account initialization waits once; later calls await an already-settled promise. Client, definition-refresh, and history-refresh promises coalesce concurrent work. Failed refreshes clear their in-flight promise and remain retryable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path and both coalescing fields are explicit, and the added test exercises the overlapping late-account path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Account initialization and GitHub response latency vary, but there is no uncertainty about the absence of duplicate calls because both layers explicitly retain in-flight promises.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added await delays only the formerly failing refresh and does not amplify remote work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cloud automations are disabled, signed out, or use an enterprise account during initialization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction registers one waiter on the existing account barrier. Disabled providers remain off the automation refresh path; once initialization settles, signed-out and enterprise states become unavailable without constructing a GitHub automation store.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per default provider, independent of repository, automation, or view size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single cached promise and one observable invalidation; no queues or remote-operation bursts are started by this adapter in these states.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The account result is represented by the singleton account service and the adapter's settled initialization promise. No cloud automation client or catalogue cache is allocated when the gate/account is ineligible.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: DefaultAccountService.getDefaultAccount only waits on initBarrier and returns current state, while the adapter's store construction is gated on enabled, non-enterprise account state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The account provider's pre-existing initialization duration can vary, but this call only waits on its Barrier and does not initiate that provider refresh.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The unconditional constructor call adds only a constant promise/barrier waiter and no filesystem or network work in disabled or ineligible states.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced constructor initialization, observable invalidation, manual refresh, downstream repository discovery, GitHub API fan-out, caching, serialization, concurrency limits, and disabled/ineligible states. No actionable performance regression was introduced.
